## 1. GLOBAL MACRO OVERVIEW

The macro backdrop is dominated by elevated inflation, a hawkish pivot risk at the Federal Reserve under new Chair Kevin Warsh, and the geopolitical premium baked into energy markets. US CPI stands at 3.95% YoY as of April [Source: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/CPIAUCSL], while PPI is running at 2.66% MoM [Source: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/PPIACO] — both well above the Fed's 2% target. The Fed Funds effective rate sits at 3.64% [Source: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/FEDFUNDS], with markets now pricing a 40% probability of a rate hike at the December FOMC meeting, up sharply from 3% probability at the June meeting [Source: https://www.cbsnews.com/news/kevin-warsh-federal-reserve-inflation-challenges/].

Treasury yields reflect this hawkish repricing. The 10-year yield is at 4.56% and the 2-year at 4.13% as of May 22 [Source: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/DGS10], producing a positively-sloped yield curve of approximately 43bps. New Fed Chair Kevin Warsh was sworn in last Friday and inherits an economy where Iran War-driven energy inflation is the primary barrier to easing. Some analysts, including Citi Research's Rob Rowe, still expect a September rate cut, while Maybank Group Wealth Management believes markets are mispricing the hike probability — arguing Warsh will adopt a "wait-and-see" posture [Source: https://www.cnbc.com/video/2026/05/25/the-market-shouldnt-be-pricing-in-a-us-rate-hike-at-the-moment-maybank-group-wealth-management.html].

Equity markets are resilient, with S&P 500 futures pointing to 7,559 [Source: https://www.wsj.com/livecoverage/stock-market-today-dow-sp-500-nasdaq-05-27-2026] as Goldman Sachs raised its year-end S&P 500 target to 8,000 from 7,600, with EPS forecast of $340/share representing 24% growth in 2026 [Source: https://www.cnbc.com/2026/05/27/goldman-raises-its-sp-500-year-end-forecast-its-for-one-simple-reason.html]. The AI semiconductor rally is a key driver, with South Korean chip maker SK Hynix rallying more than 9% to hit the $1 trillion market cap milestone, following Micron's achievement just the prior session [Source: https://www.wsj.com/livecoverage/stock-market-today-dow-sp-500-nasdaq-05-27-2026].

The VIX stands at 17.04 [Source: Yahoo Finance (^VIX)], reflecting moderate rather than acute fear — consistent with a market that is digesting multiple risks but retaining its structural bid. The ECB warned Wednesday that financial markets are underestimating geopolitical and fiscal risks, characterising market moves in response to the Iran conflict as "orderly" but reflecting "complacency" [Source: https://www.wsj.com/pro/central-banking/financial-markets-underestimate-geopolitical-and-fiscal-risks-ecb-warns-55e8f322]. The US dollar (DXY at 99.10) [Source: Yahoo Finance (DX-Y.NYB)] is in recovery mode from early May lows, but technical analysis identifies a key breakout level above 100.60, with a right shoulder of a potential inverse head-and-shoulders pattern forming around 97.60/65 [Source: https://www.kitco.com/news/off-the-wire/2026-05-26/mapping-market-big-test-dollars-recovery-approaching].

Australia's April CPI came in at 4.2% YoY, below the 4.4% expected, and down from 4.6% prior [Source: https://www.fxstreet.com/news/australia-cpi-expected-to-remain-well-above-rba-target-in-april-202605261900] — a modest positive surprise but still well above the RBA's 2-3% target band. The Reserve Bank of New Zealand held its OCR at 2.25% for the third consecutive meeting but signalled hikes are coming, with the vote split 3-3 among committee members [Source: https://www.wsj.com/economy/central-banking/new-zealands-central-bank-narrowly-votes-to-hold-rates-signals-hikes-are-coming-68a31f60].
